SKIN — the most-repeated failure: every previous attempt came back orange. Use exactly five desaturated tones and nothing more saturated: pale pink-beige highlight, light peach, muted rose midtone, mauve-brown shadow, and a lifted grey-plum deepest shadow that is still clearly LIGHT. Never apricot, never salmon, never coral, never tan, never crushed to black. Warm amber appears ONLY as a few broken one-block edge highlights, never spread across the face.

Draw this as a TRUE LOW-RESOLUTION PIXEL SPRITE that has been enlarged with NEAREST-NEIGHBOUR, not as a smooth illustration and not as a polished painting shrunk down. Build it on a coarse grid of about 190x230 art pixels and blow every art pixel up into a solid square of ONE flat colour about 5-6 canvas pixels wide, all squares the same size, all aligned to one single grid. Every diagonal, every curve and every contour therefore reads as a visible hard STAIRCASE of those squares. There must be no in-between colour anywhere in the image: no anti-aliased edge pixels, no soft colour ramps, no airbrushed cheeks, no gradient fills, no glossy specular blobs, no blur, no strand-by-strand hair, no thin tapering lines, no line thinner than one block, no speckled noise, no scattered stray single pixels. Each material gets only 4-6 flat tones arranged as LARGE CONNECTED hard-edged clusters — a cheek is one shape, a fold is one shape — plus a clean dark contour one block thick around the figure and around the major shapes. An ordered checkerboard of two tones is the ONLY permitted blend. The whole image uses at most about 28 colours. This is emphatically NOT anime, NOT manga, NOT vector lineart, NOT a semi-realistic digital painting — it is the deliberate, blocky, hand-placed pixel work of the reference image.
LIGHT — restrained, one warm overhead key. Lit planes (forehead, nose ridge, upper cheeks, the tops of shoulders and folds) take the light tones, and clear muted shadow CLUSTERS sit under the cap or hair, under the chin, in the eye sockets and under the collar, so every plane separates. FRAMING: head-and-shoulders bust, centred, facing the viewer from slightly below eye level like a Coffee Talk customer across the counter. The ENTIRE figure — hair, hat, both shoulders, both upper arms and anything held — sits inside the canvas with clear empty space above the head and at least 8% of the canvas width of empty background beyond the widest point on the left and on the right. The figure is cut ONLY by the bottom edge, across the chest. Nothing touches or is clipped by the top, left or right edge.

NEVER paint a grey-and-white checkerboard to fake transparency, that is a hard rejection. The figure must meet the background with a HARD one-block edge; no soft, feathered or semi-transparent halo of any kind may surround the silhouette, because the pipeline keys that colour out and any haze survives as a dirty fringe.
No text, no lettering, no watermark, no signature, no border, no frame, no UI chrome, no brand marks or logos on any garment or object.
PALETTE BUDGET (hard, and the axis every round has failed on): the finished image must contain AT MOST 28 distinct colours in total, and every single one of them must cover a large connected area — no colour may exist as a handful of scattered pixels or as a one-block transition between two other colours. Budget them before you draw: about 5 for skin, 4-5 for hair, 4-5 for the main garment, 3 for the accent colour, 3-4 for the props, 2 for the contour. If a shape needs a shade you have not budgeted, use the nearest budgeted one instead. The test a viewer applies: pick any pixel, and it must belong to a cluster of at least a dozen identical neighbours.
